html:
Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1421 to 1451, with a short break, and the father of Mehmed II, the conqueror of Constantinople. He rebuilt Ottoman power after the defeat by Timur and set up the conquests of his son.

  • In 1422 he besieged Constantinople to punish the Byzantines for backing a rival claimant, but had to break off.
  • In 1430 he took Thessalonica from Venice (siege of Thessalonica).
  • He fought Hungary and the Serbs, and faced the rising of Skanderbeg in Albania from 1443.

In 1444 he made peace with Hungary and stepped down in favour of Mehmed, then twelve years old. A Christian crusade broke the truce at once, and Murad came back to command. At the Battle of Varna that November he crushed the crusaders and killed the young king of Poland and Hungary. The failure of Byzantine hopes for Western help, which John VIII Palaiologos had sought at a church council in Italy, was now plain.

He took the throne back in 1446, broke through the Hexamilion wall across the Isthmus of Corinth into the Morea, and beat the Hungarian general John Hunyadi at Kosovo in 1448. He was a patron of poets and scholars. He died in Edirne in 1451; two years later his son took the city that Constantine XI still held.
sum: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1421 to 1451, with a short break, and the father of Mehmed II, the conqueror of Constantinople. He rebuilt Ottoman power after the defeat by Timur and set up the conquests of his son.
